reason: The contract (problem.txt) requires each output component to satisfy abs(actual-target) <= 1e-7 + 5e-7*|target| over EVERY finite FP16 component combination, and permits any internal algorithm only if it meets this. Confirmed in-scope runtime evidence shows the kernel's Smith-algorithm FP32 numerators violate this on legal, exactly representable FP16 inputs: (c1, probe t13) with |c|~|d| (~0.99) and a,b ~ ±65504 near-cancelling the real numerator, 99 of 600 components violate the tolerance with worst abs_err 7.1e-4 against tol 1.7e-7 (err_over_tol ~4250); (c2, probe t14) even simple exact inputs like num=[-29776,65504], den=[11,5] give real-component error 6.7e-5 vs tolerance 1.5e-7 (err_over_tol ~432), with 7 of 8 sweep cases violating. These failures stem from catastrophic cancellation and ratio-rounding amplification in the kernel's tl.fma/div_rn FP32 path (kernel.py lines 18-26), not from any contract-sanctioned deviation: the tolerance clause explicitly states the error budget 'does not depend on the magnitude of the other component' and that internal precision is only permitted if the tolerance is met. The reference FP64 computation is finite and well-defined at these inputs, so this is a genuine correctness failure, not a reference-undefined case. Claim c3 (subnormal-denominator overflow to inf) was rebutted: the maximum possible FP16-domain quotient magnitude (~1.1e12) is far below FP32 max, and the kernel produced finite, exactly correct outputs there. Skeptic reviewed all evidence and recorded no new claims. Reject on c1 and c2.
